324	func runDoctor(cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, jsonOut, verbose bool, failOn string) error {
325		failOn, err := normalizeDoctorFailOn(failOn)
326		if err != nil {
327			return err
328		}
329		env := opts.Env
330		report := doctorReport{Env: map[string]string{
331			"ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION":       env.CLIVersion,
332			"ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT":         env.RepoRoot,
333			"ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR": env.PluginConfigDir,
334			"ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR":   env.PluginDataDir,
335			"ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR":  env.PluginStateDir,
336			"ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR":  env.PluginCacheDir,
337		}}
338		dirs, err := base.ResolvePluginDirs(env)
339		if err != nil {
340			return err
341		}
342		for _, check := range []struct {
343			label string
344			path  string
345		}{
346			{label: "plugin config dir", path: dirs.Config},
347			{label: "plugin data dir", path: dirs.Data},
348			{label: "plugin state dir", path: dirs.State},
349			{label: "plugin cache dir", path: dirs.Cache},
350		} {
351			health := inspectAbsoluteInstallDirectory(check.path)
352			report.DirectoryHealth = append(report.DirectoryHealth, health)
353			report.Dirs = append(report.Dirs, doctorDirectoryFinding(check.label, health))
354		}
355		repoRoot, repoRootSource := doctorRepoRoot(cmd.Context(), opts)
356		report.RepoRoot = repoRoot
357		report.RepoRootSource = repoRootSource
358		switch {
359		case repoRoot == "":
360			// Say so, and say what to do. Silence here is what made doctor look
361			// broken rather than out of scope.
362			// Environment-scoped: "you ran me somewhere without a repository" is a
363			// statement about the invocation, not a finding about any brain's
364			// health, and it must not fail a gate on one.
365			report.Checks = append(report.Checks, doctorCheckResult{
366				Name:   "repo",
367				State:  "warn",
368				Scope:  doctorScopeEnvironment,
369				Detail: "no repository in scope: " + base.EnvRepoRoot + " is unset and the working directory is not inside a git work tree; run doctor from inside the repository, or set " + base.EnvRepoRoot,
370			})
371		case opts.Runner == nil:
372			report.Checks = append(report.Checks, doctorCheckResult{
373				Name:   "repo",
374				State:  "warn",
375				Scope:  doctorScopeEnvironment,
376				Detail: "no command runner: repo-scoped checks skipped for " + repoRoot,
377			})
378		}
379		if repoRoot != "" && opts.Runner != nil {
380			// The repo-scoped helpers below read opts.Env for storage identity, so
381			// the inferred root has to travel in the copy they get -- otherwise an
382			// inferred run would report on the repo it found but resolve storage as
383			// if no repo were selected at all.
384			scoped := opts
385			scoped.Env.RepoRoot = repoRoot
386			opts = scoped
387			env = scoped.Env
388			report.Checks, report.Memory = brainDoctorReadOnlyReport(cmd.Context(), opts, repoRoot)
389			// Whatever the last `setup` could not build. setup keeps going on a
390			// component failure and points here for the reason, so the reason has to
391			// actually be here.
392			if storage, serr := repoStoragePaths(cmd.Context(), opts.Runner, env, repoRoot); serr == nil {
393				for _, component := range failedSetupComponents(filepath.Dir(storage.HeadPath), storage.BrainDir) {
394					detail := component.Detail
395					if hint := component.Hint; hint != "" {
396						detail += "; " + hint
397					}
398					report.Checks = append(report.Checks, doctorCheckResult{
399						Name:   "setup " + setupComponentLabel(component.Name),
400						State:  "error",
401						Detail: detail,
402					})
403				}
404			}
405			// The full blind-spot list lives HERE. `status` collapses forty-four
406			// per-file warnings into one line and tells the reader to run doctor for
407			// the detail, so the detail has to actually exist somewhere — and doctor
408			// is the right somewhere: it is the command you run when you have decided
409			// to care.
410			if spots, spotErr := brainBlindSpotsForRepo(cmd.Context(), opts, repoRoot); spotErr == nil {
411				for _, group := range groupStatusBlindSpots(spots) {
412					report.Checks = append(report.Checks, doctorCheckResult{
413						Name:   "semantic blind spots",
414						State:  "warn",
415						Detail: group.Summary() + ": " + strings.Join(group.Paths, ", "),
416					})
417				}
418			}
419			if semReport, semErr := semanticStaleReport(cmd.Context(), opts, repoRoot); semErr != nil {
420				report.Checks = append(report.Checks, doctorCheckResult{Name: "semantic", State: "warn", Detail: "unavailable: " + semErr.Error()})
421			} else {
422				report.Checks = append(report.Checks, semanticDoctorFindings(semReport)...)
423				if coverage, err := doctorSemanticCoverage(cmd.Context(), opts, repoRoot, semReport); err != nil {
424					report.Checks = append(report.Checks, doctorCheckResult{Name: "semantic coverage", State: "warn", Detail: err.Error()})
425				} else {
426					report.SemanticCoverage = coverage
427				}
428			}
429		}
430		if jsonOut {
431			if err := cmdutil.WriteJSON(cmd, report); err != nil {
432				return err
433			}
434			return doctorGateResult(report, failOn)
435		}
436		out := cmd.OutOrStdout()
437		if verbose {
438			renderDoctorVerbose(out, report)
439		} else {
440			renderDoctorActionable(out, report)
441		}
442		return doctorGateResult(report, failOn)
443	}

445	// doctorVerboseInvocation is the one command that turns the short report back
446	// into the long one. It is named on every short report, so the detail a reader
447	// does not see is always one documented command away.
448	// A func, not a const: the spelling is only knowable at call time.
449	func doctorVerboseInvocation() string {
450		return base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "doctor --verbose")
451	}
452	
453	// doctorActionableDetailBudget caps one short line's detail. The blind-spot
454	// groups carry every skipped path -- 3.5KB on this repository alone -- which is
455	// a list to read at leisure under --verbose, not a wall to scroll past when you
456	// are looking for what to fix.
457	const doctorActionableDetailBudget = 160
458	
459	// renderDoctorVerbose is the whole report: the environment doctor read, the
460	// resolved repository, and every finding at full detail, passing or not.
461	func renderDoctorVerbose(out io.Writer, report doctorReport) {
462		for _, key := range []string{"ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION", "ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT", "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR", "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR", "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR", "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR"} {
463			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s=%s\n", key, valueOrUnset(report.Env[key]))
464		}
465		if report.RepoRoot != "" && report.RepoRootSource != base.EnvRepoRoot {
466			fmt.Fprintf(out, "repo root: %s (inferred from %s)\n", report.RepoRoot, report.RepoRootSource)
467		}
468		for _, dir := range report.Dirs {
469			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s: %s (%s)\n", dir.Name, dir.State, dir.Detail)
470		}
471		for _, check := range report.Checks {
472			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s: %s", check.Name, check.State)
473			if check.Detail != "" {
474				fmt.Fprintf(out, " (%s)", check.Detail)
475			}
476			fmt.Fprintln(out)
477		}
478		// Coverage is counts, never a finding: it names nothing to fix, so it
479		// belongs with the rest of the passing detail under --verbose. The one
480		// coverage condition a reader can act on -- the audit failing -- is a
481		// "semantic coverage" warn check above, and the short report prints it.
482		if c := report.SemanticCoverage; c != nil {
483			fmt.Fprintf(out, "semantic coverage: %d files, %d symbols, %d relations (manifest counts)\n", c.Files, c.Symbols, c.Relations)
484			for _, section := range []struct {
485				name   string
486				counts []semanticAuditCount
487			}{
488				{"file languages", c.FileLanguages}, {"symbol languages", c.Languages},
489				{"symbol kinds", c.SymbolKinds}, {"relation types", c.RelationTypes},
490			} {
491				if len(section.counts) > 0 {
492					fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s: %s\n", section.name, semanticAuditCountSummary(section.counts))
493				}
494			}
495		}
496	}

498	// renderDoctorActionable is the default report, and it prints exactly the
499	// findings a reader can do something about.
500	//
501	// The old default printed six environment lines, four passing directory lines
502	// and every passing check -- forty lines and 6.4KB on a HEALTHY brain, of which
503	// six said anything and exactly one named a remedy. A diagnostic that cries
504	// wolf on a healthy system teaches people to stop reading it, and then the one
505	// line that mattered is lost in the thirty-four that did not.
506	//
507	// So: nothing that passed, and every line that did not ends with a command.
508	// The counts stay, because "I printed nothing" and "I checked nothing" must not
509	// look the same, and the summary names the flag that restores the long form.
510	//
511	// Non-ok findings are NEVER dropped or capped. A brain with twelve problems
512	// prints twelve lines; the saving comes from silence about what is fine, not
513	// from hiding what is broken.
514	func renderDoctorActionable(out io.Writer, report doctorReport) {
515		okCount, warnCount, errorCount := 0, 0, 0
516		var lines []doctorActionableLine
517		for i, dir := range report.Dirs {
518			switch dir.State {
519			case "ok":
520				okCount++
521				continue
522			case "warn":
523				warnCount++
524			default:
525				errorCount++
526			}
527			// Dirs and DirectoryHealth are appended in lockstep, so the health that
528			// produced this finding -- and the path to chmod -- is at the same index.
529			var health memoryInstallDirectoryHealth
530			if i < len(report.DirectoryHealth) {
531				health = report.DirectoryHealth[i]
532			}
533			lines = append(lines, doctorActionableLine{finding: dir, remedy: doctorDirectoryRemedy(health)})
534		}
535		for _, check := range report.Checks {
536			switch check.State {
537			case "ok":
538				okCount++
539				continue
540			case "warn":
541				warnCount++
542			default:
543				errorCount++
544			}
545			lines = append(lines, doctorActionableLine{finding: check, remedy: doctorRemedy(check)})
546		}
547		if len(lines) == 0 {
548			fmt.Fprintf(out, "healthy: %d check(s) passed, nothing to fix; run `%s` for the full report\n", okCount, doctorVerboseInvocation())
549			return
550		}
551		for _, line := range lines {
552			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s: %s (%s)\n", line.finding.Name, line.finding.State, line.detail())
553		}
554		fmt.Fprintf(out, "%d ok, %d warn, %d error; run `%s` for the full report\n", okCount, warnCount, errorCount, doctorVerboseInvocation())
555	}

557	// doctorActionableLine is one short-report line: the finding, and the command
558	// that addresses it when the finding's own detail does not already name one.
559	type doctorActionableLine struct {
560		finding doctorCheckResult
561		remedy  string
562	}
563	
564	func (l doctorActionableLine) detail() string {
565		detail := truncateDoctorDetail(l.finding.Detail)
566		// Whether the detail names its own command is decided on the text that is
567		// actually PRINTED. Deciding it on the untruncated detail meant a line
568		// whose command had been cut in half still suppressed the remedy, and the
569		// reader got "...; run `entire brain ref…" and nothing else.
570		// Truncation never cuts inside a span, so a backtick here means a whole one.
571		if strings.Contains(detail, "`") {
572			return detail
573		}
574		if l.remedy == "" {
575			return detail
576		}
577		if detail == "" {
578			return "run `" + l.remedy + "`"
579		}
580		return strings.TrimRight(detail, "; ") + "; run `" + l.remedy + "`"
581	}
582	
583	func truncateDoctorDetail(detail string) string {
584		runes := []rune(detail)
585		if len(runes) <= doctorActionableDetailBudget {
586			return detail
587		}
588		cut := doctorActionableDetailBudget
589		// Never cut inside a `command` span. Half a command is worse than none: it
590		// cannot be run, and it still looks like the line answered the question.
591		// Backticks are balanced, so an odd count before the cut means it lands
592		// inside one; back up to that span's opening backtick and drop it whole.
593		if strings.Count(string(runes[:cut]), "`")%2 == 1 {
594			for cut > 0 && runes[cut-1] != '`' {
595				cut--
596			}
597			cut--
598		}
599		if cut < 0 {
600			cut = 0
601		}
602		kept := strings.TrimRight(string(runes[:cut]), " ,;`")
603		// Dropping the command can leave the word that introduced it, so the line
604		// read "...; run\u2026; run `entire brain refresh`". Trim the dangling lead-in.
605		for _, lead := range []string{"; run", " run", "; try", " try"} {
606			kept = strings.TrimSuffix(kept, lead)
607		}
608		return strings.TrimRight(kept, " ,;") + "\u2026"
609	}
610	
611	// doctorDirectoryRemedy: every non-ok plugin-directory finding is a permission
612	// or path problem on a named directory, and the mode bits are the part doctor
613	// can actually see.
614	func doctorDirectoryRemedy(health memoryInstallDirectoryHealth) string {
615		// The remedy is rendered as "run `<remedy>`", so it must be something a
616		// reader can actually run.
617		//
618		// This used to return health.RecommendedAction whenever it was set, which
619		// a previous finding asked for. Every constructor seeds that field and then
620		// overwrites it on each path, so it is NEVER empty for a real doctor run:
621		// the branches below were unreachable outside hand-built fixtures, and the
622		// line rendered as
623		//
624		//   run `grant write access before running a mutation; mode bits currently deny writes`
625		//
626		// presenting a sentence as a command, which is the defect this whole
627		// report set out to remove.
628		//
629		// Nothing is lost by not repeating it here: doctorDirectoryFinding already
630		// puts that guidance in the Detail this remedy is appended to, either in
631		// its own words for the two warn states or verbatim for the error state.
632		path := strings.TrimSpace(health.Path)
633		if path == "" {
634			return doctorVerboseInvocation()
635		}
636		if strings.Contains(health.State, "unsafe") {
637			// A symlink, a non-directory, or a relative path. No mode change fixes
638			// any of them, and what the reader needs first is to see what is there.
639			return "ls -ld " + shellQuote(path)
640		}
641		if !health.Exists {
642			// The detail names the nearest EXISTING parent as the thing denying
643			// writes, so that is what the reader has to change. filepath.Dir climbs
644			// exactly one level, which was wrong whenever more than one component
645			// was missing -- the default data dir is three levels deep, so the
646			// suggested chmod named a directory that did not exist either.
647			return "chmod u+w " + shellQuote(nearestExistingAncestor(path))
648		}
649		return "chmod u+w " + shellQuote(path)
650	}
651	
652	// shellQuote makes a path safe to paste into a shell.
653	//
654	// Raised as a shell-injection finding. As stated the threat model is weak: the
655	// path comes from the reader's OWN ENTIRE_PLUGIN_* variables or home directory,
656	// and anyone who can set those can already run code. The quoting is right for a
657	// duller reason that bites far more often — a path containing a SPACE produces a
658	// command that silently chmods the wrong thing, and "/Users/me/My Brain" is an
659	// ordinary path on a Mac.
660	//
661	// Single quotes, because inside them a shell expands nothing at all; an embedded
662	// single quote is closed, escaped and reopened.
663	func shellQuote(s string) string {
664		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
665	}
666	
667	// doctorRemedies maps a finding to the command that addresses it, for the
668	// findings whose detail does not already quote one.
669	//

716		"memory_sessions":        "refresh sessions",
717		"memory_reconciliation":  "memory reconcile",
718		// Host-environment findings. entire-brain neither installs nor repairs the
719		// Entire CLI or the Graph provider, so the command is the one the README
720		// gives for installing them -- not an entire-brain verb that would quietly
721		// do nothing.
722		"memory_install": "curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash",
723		// "semantic provider" is deliberately ABSENT: its remedy depends on which
724		// side of the pair is behind, which a name-keyed table cannot express.
725		// See doctorSemanticProviderRemedy.
726		// Quoted: unquoted, `<your` is an input redirection and the line fails with
727		// a redirection error instead of saying anything. A placeholder still has
728		// to survive being pasted.
729		"repo": "cd '<your repository>' && entire brain doctor",

732	func doctorRemedy(check doctorCheckResult) string {
733		// The "detail already names a command" case is NOT decided here: it depends
734		// on the truncated text, which only doctorActionableLine.detail sees.
735		// `setup <component>` findings are one per failed setup component.
736		if strings.HasPrefix(check.Name, "setup ") {
737			return base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "setup")
738		}
739		if check.Name == doctorSemanticProviderFinding {
740			return doctorSemanticProviderRemedy(check.Detail)
741		}
742		if verb, ok := doctorRemedies[check.Name]; ok {
743			return base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, verb)
744		}
745		// A check added later without a table entry still gets a command, because
746		// "no remedy" is the one answer a diagnostic must never give.
747		return doctorVerboseInvocation()
748	}
749	
750	// doctorSemanticProviderRemedy picks the remedy for the ONE finding whose fix
751	// depends on the condition rather than on the finding's name.
752	//
753	// "semantic provider" reports a pair that has to agree: this build of
754	// entire-brain and the entire-graph provider it reads. Either side can be the
755	// one that is behind, and the table above is keyed by finding NAME, so it
756	// could only ever name one of them. It named Graph. That is right when the
757	// provider is absent and exactly backwards on a version skew, where the
758	// provider is the side that is AHEAD:
759	//
760	//	semantic provider: warn (provider=degraded (semantic provider emitted
761	//	schema_version "1.3" but this build reads 1.1; ...; but upgrade
762	//	entire-b...; run `entire plugin install graph`)
763	//
764	// The message says upgrade Brain and the remedy says install Graph. Installing
765	// Graph cannot help, and a newer Graph widens the skew it was offered for.
766	//
767	// Like every other classification of a provider failure here, this one reads
768	// the FULL detail, never the truncated line: truncation cuts the skew message
769	// mid-word ("upgrade entire-b..."), so a remedy chosen from what is printed
770	// would flip back to the wrong side exactly when the line is long enough to
771	// need the help.
772	func doctorSemanticProviderRemedy(detail string) string {
773		if doctorSemanticProviderAhead(detail) {
774			return doctorBrainUpgradeRemedy
775		}
776		return doctorGraphInstallRemedy
777	}
778	
779	// doctorSemanticProviderAhead reports whether the detail describes a provider
780	// that is NEWER than this build, i.e. the skew where entire-brain is the side
781	// to upgrade. It matches the remedy the message itself states, so the two can
782	// only disagree if someone rewords the message without rewording this.
783	func doctorSemanticProviderAhead(detail string) bool {
784		text := strings.ToLower(detail)
785		return strings.Contains(text, "upgrade entire-brain")
786	}
787	
788	// doctorGateResult wraps a tripped gate the way `status --fail-on` does: the
789	// report is already on stdout and names every failing check, so the error is
790	// marked rendered and the process exits nonzero without printing a second,
791	// less informative copy of the same news to stderr.
792	func doctorGateResult(report doctorReport, failOn string) error {
793		if err := doctorGateFailure(report, failOn); err != nil {
794			return renderedCommandError{err: err}
795		}
796		return nil
797	}
798	
799	// nearestExistingAncestor walks up until it finds a directory that exists.
800	// inspectAbsoluteInstallDirectory's creatable_unproven state can sit under
801	// arbitrarily many missing components, and a chmod against one of those fails
802	// with "No such file or directory" rather than fixing anything.
803	//
804	// Returns the last path examined if it runs out of ancestors, so the caller
805	// always has something to name.
806	func nearestExistingAncestor(path string) string {
807		dir := filepath.Dir(path)
808		for {
809			if info, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
810				return dir
811			}
812			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
813			if parent == dir {
814				return dir
815			}
816			dir = parent
817		}
818	}

# Git

description.description:

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

refactor(cli): move version and capabilities commands into internal/cli/command/{version,capabilities}

agent_setup_test.go, a root-routing test that stays in cli, decodes the
JSON contract into them.

command and depends on cli-private fixtures (fakeCommandRunner, execute,
evalCommandFailWriter) shared by the rest of the suite; only symbol
qualification changed. runnable_remedies_test.go drops its
capabilities.go allowlist entry: the static scan reads only
internal/cli/*.go, so the moved file is outside its scope (the entities
extraction set this precedent); the hardcoded machine-contract strings
remain pinned by capabilities_report_regression_test.go.

doctor and path stay in cli for this wave; their closures exceed the
split budget (doctor reads 18 cli-private symbols across nine files,
path drives runRefresh and the repo-storage-set machinery).

EOF
)" && git log -1 --format='%H %s'

content.text:
## Report — COR-2268 system-command cluster

**Branch / commit:** `cor-2268-cmd-system` @ `83b5fb5b` (from `cor-2268-cmdutil`). Not pushed.

**Preflights:** Brain v0.3.0-17-g98a7c172 and Graph entire-graph v0.6.0 both available; brief run. One Graph gap: `impact` could not resolve the unexported Go consts (`brainCGOBuild`, `retrievalSourceFact`) — fuzzy-matched unrelated JSON/Markdown sections — so consumer enumeration for unexported symbols fell back to grep, which the recipe permits.

**Moved (prod):**
- `internal/cli/version.go` → `internal/cli/command/version/version.go`, `version.New(version string)` — IDENTICAL under rename map (`newVersionCommand`→`New`).
- `internal/cli/capabilities.go` → `internal/cli/command/capabilities/capabilities.go`, `capabilities.New(opts base.Options)` — IDENTICAL under rename map (+2 import lines). `brainCapabilities`/`brainSourceCapability` exported (`BrainCapabilities`/`BrainSourceCapability`) because `agent_setup_test.go`, a root-routing test staying in cli, decodes the JSON contract into them.
- `root.go` registrations updated; new packages import only base/brainstore/sqlitedriver — never `internal/cli`.

**Helpers sunk (grep evidence, per-file counts cited in-session):**
- `brainCGOBuild` → `sqlitedriver.BrainCGO`; `sqlite_driver_purego.go` deleted; call sites: memory_admin.go + 2 tests.
- `retrievalSourceAll/Fact/History/Conversation/Doc` → `brainstore.RetrievalSource*` (new `brainstore/retrieval_sources.go`, comment verbatim); all 20 cli files renamed (6 prod, 14 test).

**Tests:** none moved. `capabilities_report_regression_test.go` stays in cli — it drives `NewRootCommand` and depends on cli-private fixtures (`fakeCommandRunner`, `execute`, `evalCommandFailWriter`) shared by hundreds of cli tests; moving it would mean duplicating or mass-sinking fixtures. Only symbol-qualification edits applied (`newCapabilitiesCommand`→`capabilities.New`, `brainCGOBuild`→`sqlitedriver.BrainCGO`). Inventory: before 3252 roots in ./internal/cli, after 3252, diff empty — IDENTICAL. New packages report `[no test files]`, so no `main_test.go` was created.

**Did not fit the rules (left in cli):**
- **doctor** — closure spans 18 cli-private symbols across nine files (`doctorCheckResult`/`brainDoctorReadOnlyReport` in lifecycle_ops.go, `memoryInstallDirectoryHealth`/`inspectAbsoluteInstallDirectory` in memory_admin.go, `staleReport`/`semanticStaleReport`/`brainBlindSpotsForRepo` in semantic.go, `repoStoragePaths` (34 prod files) and `valueOrUnset` (14) in env.go, `loadGraphManifest`, `failedSetupComponents`/`setupComponentLabel`, `groupStatusBlindSpots`, `semanticAudit*`, `renderedCommandError`). Far over the ~3 budget.
